answer: A registry can require each agent to lock a bond that rises quadratically with the number of identities sharing one attestation root: the first locks 30 tokens for 16 epochs, the second 120, the third 270, so a mesa of fake accounts quickly becomes unaffordable. Before earning, each identity must pass three peer audits in separate rounds, and the shale layer of on-chain receipts proves every lock and audit. An opal badge is issued only after all audits pass, and any failed audit slashes 25 percent of the bond, so each extra fake identity costs far more than the capped reward it could earn.
